denominator_rule: Every tool the deep-dive concluded BLOCKED, partitioned into root-cause problems. The partition is MECE and was verified by script: 65 assigned, 65 distinct, 0 missing, 0 duplicated. A problem is never merged, split, reordered or dropped for cost. If a re-run moves a tool to a different problem, it moves — the total never shrinks except by a tool reaching proven.
ordering_rule: sort by (a) tools in the cluster whose MEASURED outcome was a FALSE STATEMENT REACHING THE AUTHOR, desc; then (b) tools the problem blocks, desc; then (c) problem id, asc. Computed, never typed. A tool that cannot be measured costs the loop time; a tool that lies to the author costs the author their work. NOTE: tie-break (c) is a STRING sort, so P10 and P11 precede P9 among the one-tool problems. The cycle numbers in this file are OUTPUT of the rule, recomputed by scripts/toolloop/problem_remaining.py — they are never hand-typed, and the first version of this file had them wrong because I typed them.
cleared_definition: A problem is CLEARED when all four hold. (1) Its invariant is NAMED. (2) The invariant is enforced at ONE chokepoint, with a falsifier proven RED on an ORIGINAL instance and the full suite green. (3) EVERY tool in the cluster has been re-run LIVE at K>=5 and now reads proven, or reads blocked on a DIFFERENT, NAMED cause — which moves it to another problem and is recorded as such. (4) The write-up states what the fix does NOT cover.

spend_policy.decision: OWNER, 2026-08-22: a confirm card for a DESTRUCTIVE or COST-BEARING tool MAY be approved when the target was created by the run's own throwaway fixture and is torn down after. Never against the dogfood book, never against a pre-existing object.

What is bounded is WASTE: the cheapest configured model, the smallest legitimate unit of work, and a card approved at most ONCE per tool per cycle — the second approval proves idempotency and is the only repeat. Every approved paid card records the model, the unit and the observed cost in its ledger row.

IT DOES NOT REACH A TOOL WHOSE REFUSAL NAMES NOTHING. IT CANNOT HELP glossary_entity_restore. No supplier exists: a soft-deleted entity is invisible to glossary search, chapter text and project memory, so there is nothing to name and nothing to arm. THE ARMING IS CAPPED AT 3 AND RANKS BY NAME LENGTH. A refusal naming four or more catalogue tools arms only three of them, chosen by a rule that has nothing to do with which one unblocks the call.

FIVE TOOLS, ONE SHAPE, AND THE DEPTH IS THE POINT. Each was re-run LIVE at K>=5 on 2026-08-23 with a fixture that reaches its state, and each fails on an id no tool on its surface can supply.

  glossary_create_evidence   needs attr_value_id      <- glossary_get_entity        advertised 0/130

  plan_bootstrap_apply       needs proposal_id        <- plan_bootstrap_propose      0 of 21 passes
  composition_reference_update needs reference_id     <- composition_find_references ADVERTISED,

THE MECHANISM. R1 answerability forces onto the wire the tool whose declared vocabulary answers the request. Nothing forces the tools THAT tool needs. A user names a GOAL, not an intermediate step, so a supplier reaches the wire only by accident - and the tiers refute the obvious explanation: 'the budget favours writes over reads' fits two pairs and fails the other two (plan apply/propose are both Tier A; arc_template get/list are both Tier R). AND THE FIX MUST BE TRANSITIVE. composition_reference_update proves it: level 1 was already on the wire and the turn still died at level 2. A one-hop 'force the supplier too' would have looked correct on the other four and left this one exactly as broken.

THE PLATFORM ALREADY HOLDS THE ANSWER FOR AT LEAST ONE. contracts/agent-runtime-tool-contracts.json declares plan_bootstrap_apply => {proposal_id: plan_bootstrap_propose} as DATA, and does not use it to put the supplier on the wire. problems.diagnosis:
TWO OF THE THREE TOOLS WERE NEVER THIS PROBLEM, and the third is it exactly.

kg_triage_schema_write is PROVEN (2026-08-23). It was never describing instead of recording - its fixture had never adopted an ontology, so every call answered 'this project has no adopted ontology to edit'. Seed the ontology and it records: called 5/5, ok:true 5/5, and the confirm token applies ({'applied': true, 'schema_version': 2}). glossary_propose_translation was already proven.

propose_edit IS the invariant, measured 2026-08-23 at K=5 with zero errored runs and the same shape every run: book_read, then THREE ALTERNATIVE REWRITES WRITTEN OUT IN THE REPLY. Called 0/5.

The request is 'Make the opening line of this chapter darker - SHOW ME THE CHANGE before it goes in', and propose_edit declares 'show me the change' verbatim. Against the live catalogue answerable_tools returns EXACTLY {propose_edit} for that sentence. It is a FRONTEND tool in the ALWAYS-ON CORE, so it is advertised on every pass of every turn - it cannot lose a hot-seed slot and cannot be gated out. It was in front of the model the whole time.

🔴 SO THE COMPETITION IS NOT ANOTHER TOOL. Nothing else was called. What beat the tool is the model's own prose, which is always available, always cheaper, and always looks like an answer. That is what makes this problem different from P5-SIBLING-WINS, where a rival tool takes the request: here there is no rival to declare precedence over.

What the user loses is precise: the rewrites are responsive and grounded (the model reads the real opening line first), but 'before it goes in' is a request for the REVIEW AFFORDANCE, and the diff card that can be applied or dismissed is never offered. The author must copy text into the editor by hand - the state the tool exists to remove.

🔴 CORRECTION 2026-08-24 - THE THIRD TOOL IS NOT THIS PROBLEM EITHER, and I had the cause wrong twice.

propose_edit declares exactly two operations: PROPOSE_EDIT_OPERATIONS = ['insert_at_cursor', 'replace_selection']. Both are defined by editor state - where the caret is, what the author has selected. chat-service's EditorContext model carries book_id, chapter_id and an optional chapter_title: no selection, no range, no cursor, and no flag saying whether anything is selected at all.

So 'make the opening line darker' cannot become replace_selection without GUESSING that the author has that line highlighted. The model reads the chapter, finds the real opening line, and offers three rewrites. That is a defensible answer to a request whose affordance it cannot confirm applies - not prose winning over a tool it understood.

WHAT I HAD SAID INSTEAD, twice: first that it 'declares NO synonyms so answerability cannot reach it' - true then, fixed since, and it changed nothing; then that 'prose wins anyway' with the competition being the model's own writing. The tool's description is already as explicit as a description can be ('shown to the user with an Apply button and is NOT applied automatically - the user reviews it first'), so the second reading required the model to have understood the tool and chosen against it. It had understood the tool. What it could not do is ground the operation.

Note the shape of my own remedy attempts here: I added synonyms including 'rewrite the selection' and 'insert at my cursor' - phrases naming the very state the turn does not carry - and forced the tool onto the wire on every pass. Both were correct mechanically and neither could work, because the missing thing was never the tool's visibility.

Filed as D-PROPOSE-EDIT-ACTS-ON-EDITOR-STATE-THE-TURN-CANNOT-SEE.

NAMED, AND NO LONGER A PROVIDER MYSTERY. Established against the deployed build's own helpers, on the exact 12-character reasoning every silent turn carries:

    _split_safe_emit('<tool_call|>')           -> flushed, nothing held
    _extract_leaked_tool_calls('<tool_call|>') -> []       nothing to salvage

The hold is keyed on the OPENING token `<|tool_call>`; the leak is the CLOSING token `<tool_call|>`, a different string. It matches no hold position, flushes into whichever channel was open - reasoning - and the pass falls through `if not tool_frags and not leaked_calls:` as an ordinary 'the model stopped without a tool call'. Every guard is correct for the input it was given; the composite is a silent turn.

FORTY-TWO CALLS STRAIGHT AT THE PROVIDER FAILED TO REPRODUCE IT (first pass, the pass after a tool result, tool counts 2/30/80 from the real catalogue, and streaming - all zero).     memory_search(query='Emberfall <nonce>')          [immediately, and again after 3s]
      -> {'hits': [], 'count': 0, 'total': 0, 'returned': 0,
          'degraded': {'semantic': 'not_indexed'},
          'note': 'no stored knowledge matched this query - note the semantic index is not built'}

    memory_forget(fact_id='00b592...')
      -> {'invalidated': true}

That is this problem's invariant word for word: the store ACCEPTED the write and confirmed it with an id, and the read that surfaces it returns nothing. Searching for the exact nonce the write had just stored finds zero.

TWO THINGS THE PROBE SETTLES that the instance did not.

1. THE READ IS HONEST ABOUT BEING BROKEN, which is better than the catalogue instance and worth separating: it returns degraded={'semantic': 'not_indexed'} and a note saying so, rather than a bare empty list. A caller that reads the envelope can tell 'nothing matched' from 'I cannot answer'. That does not fix the invariant - hits is still [] and a model reporting count:0 tells the author there is nothing - but it means the fix here may be in how the ANSWER is composed, not in the store.

2. THE FAILURE IS THE SEARCH PATH, NOT forget. Handed the id directly, memory_forget invalidates the fact and says so. So memory_forget's membership in this problem is CORRECT and precise: what the false absence breaks is the only route a model has to the fact_id, since memory_remember's id is gone by the next turn.
problems.status:
🔴 NOW READS 'CLEARED' BY TOOL COUNT AND ITS INVARIANT STILL FAILS - the clearest instance yet of why those are different claims, and the reason the definition check exists.

BUT THE PROBLEM IS THIS PROBLEM, NOT ITS TOOLS. problems.title: The world-setup intent gate shuts on the concrete request
problems.invariant_candidate: A gate must open on WHAT THE REQUEST ASKS FOR, not on the vocabulary it happens to use.

moved_out.glossary_propose_batch:
MOVED to P5-SIBLING-WINS 2026-08-23 by the partition rule — THE GATE WAS OPEN ON ITS TURNS, so the gate is not what blocks it. Batch c-r1-recheck, K=5, ZERO errored runs: the turn's injected skills were ['co_write', 'glossary', 'glossary_shaping'], and glossary_shaping is exactly the skill filter_intent_gated_setup_tools requires — verified directly against the deployed function, which drops all five gated tools with injected=[] or ['co_write'] and keeps all five with ['glossary_shaping']. So this tool was in the turn's catalogue.

It was called 0/5 anyway: on every run the model ran glossary_list_system_standards -> glossary_adopt_standards -> glossary_task_provide_input. glossary_adopt_standards is ANOTHER of the five gated tools, surfaced by the same open gate, and it won the request. That is P5's shape, not P9's.

NOTE THE ASYMMETRY THIS EXPOSES, which is P9's actual subject: the two tools in P9 had the SAME gate and opposite outcomes, decided by the prompt's vocabulary. 'Set up several kinds and attributes at once for this book's ontology' injects glossary_shaping; 'Take the upstream changes - apply the standard updates to this book' does not.

problems.diagnosis:
THE GATE IS ALL-OR-NOTHING ON A SKILL INJECTION, AND R1 CANNOT OVERRULE IT BY CONSTRUCTION. Both halves measured 2026-08-23.

1. THE GATE ITSELF. filter_intent_gated_setup_tools, called directly against the deployed build, drops all five INTENT_GATED_SETUP_TOOLS with injected skills [] or ['co_write'] and keeps all five with ['glossary_shaping']. There is no per-tool nuance: the turn either has the setup skill or has no setup tools. So the whole question is what injects the skill, and the answer is the prompt's VOCABULARY - the two tools in this problem got opposite outcomes from the same gate (glossary_propose_batch's prompt injected it, glossary_book_sync_apply's did not), which is DQ-T31's measurement repeated on a second pair.

2. 🔴 AND THE ANSWERABILITY RESCUE CANNOT REACH A GATED TOOL - THIS IS NEW. R1 promises a tool whose declared vocabulary answers the request reaches the wire 'whatever the budget, the domain selection or the rail decided'. For glossary_book_sync_apply the request IS its vocabulary twice over ('take the upstream changes', 'apply the standard updates') and answerable_tools returns EXACTLY that one tool for it - yet chat-service's own per-pass log shows 'R1 answerability: request matches [glossary_book_sync_apply]' ONCE per turn and 34 activated tools without it on EVERY pass.

The cause is which catalogue each advertise site is handed: the ONE-OFF build gets _catalog_index(catalog) - unfiltered - and does rescue the tool; the PER-PASS build gets _catalog_index(discovery_catalog) - filtered by the gate - cannot match a tool that is not in it, and REPLACES the one-off list on the first pass. Neither piece is buggy and the guarantee still cannot hold. See D-R1-CANNOT-RESCUE-AN-INTENT-GATED-TOOL-BY-CONSTRUCTION.

WHAT THAT MEANS FOR THE FIX. DQ-T31's recommendation is to add a declaration arm to the gate, 'the rule R1 already applies at the advertise chokepoint'. It cannot be inherited for free: R1 runs at a chokepoint that no longer contains the tool. The arm has to live in the GATE, before the narrowing - or the narrowing needs an exemption like the one a pinned rail's step tools already get.
problems.status: DIAGNOSIS COMPLETE 2026-08-23, NOT CLEARED, and the fix is an OWNER decision (DQ-T31). One tool remains after glossary_propose_batch moved out on measured cause: glossary_book_sync_apply, surfaced 0/5 and called 0/5 at K=5 with zero errored runs.
